# Stop af-impl at the pushed branch

## Intent

`af-impl` ends by merging into the base branch and by opening forge issues,
which suits a person in the session and `specrun`. A controller, such as
nightshift, lands the work itself through a hub: its implementer session
cannot write the base branch and has no forge token. With `--no-merge`,
`af-impl` implements the package on the branch it was started on, pushes
that branch and stops there, and it says what it did and what it left open
in a result file whose shape is published as a JSON Schema.

## Goals

- **`af-impl` can stop at the pushed branch.** With `--no-merge` it
  implements the package on the branch it was started on, pushes that
  branch, and neither merges, nor touches the base branch, nor calls the
  forge.
- **The open items go to the caller, not to the forge.** What a landing
  would file as issues is listed in the result, each with its kind.
- **Every such run leaves a result file.** With `--result <file>` the run
  writes one JSON document that says how it ended, what it produced and
  what it left open. A caller reads that file and nothing else of the
  session.
- **The result has a published schema.**
  `specification/schemas/af-impl-result.v1.json` accepts every result a
  `--no-merge` run writes and refuses a document that breaks one of the
  rules below.

## Non-goals

- **`af-impl --rework`.** Fixing findings on finished work is the package
  `31_af_impl_rework`.
- **The `af-spec` modes.** They are the package
  `29_af_spec_under_controller`.
- **The controller.** What starts these sessions, where they run, what it
  does with a result and how the work lands is the controller's:
  `agent-fox-dev/nightshift`, `docs/prd/02-drive-work-items-through-the-hub.md`.
- **Changes to `specrun`.** It keeps calling `af-impl` as it does, and
  `af-impl` without the new arguments behaves as it does today.
- **Changes to the package format, `afspec`, `speca` or `specr`.** The mode
  uses the commands as they are.
- **Reading or writing forge issues in this mode.** The open items go to
  the result file; whoever lands the work files them.
- **A command that validates a result file.** The schema is published; a
  caller validates with a JSON Schema validator of its own.

## Background

**`af-impl`** (`skills/af-impl/SKILL.md`) implements a package and runs to
the merge. It refuses to start on the work branch (§2), creates
`feature/<NN>-<slug>` from the base branch (§4), reads open items from the
forge with `issue` in its survey (`references/survey.md`), opens an issue
for every open item, merges into the base branch on a full gate of the
merged tree, pushes the base branch and closes and relabels issues
(`references/landing.md`). It never force-pushes. Its `--unattended`
(`references/unattended.md`) runs each implement task in a subagent and
changes nothing else. A package whose tasks are all `done` or `dropped` is
refused in §2: there is nothing to implement. The open items a run leaves
are the `unmet` list of `references/conformance.md`, each with one kind
(`awaits`, `defect` with a severity, `untested`, `deviation`). Its body is
within 200 bytes of the ceiling `make skills-check` enforces (24,576 bytes,
ADR 12), so what a mode adds goes into a reference file.

**What tells a caller how a run went.** `specrun` reads git: the merge
commit on the base branch and its `AF-Run:` trailer, whose `gate` object is
copied from `speca <package> --gate-report` and whose `open_items` object
counts what the run opened, closed, passed on and reclassified. There is no
machine-readable result of a run that did not merge.

**The gate's answer.** `speca <package> --gate full` answers in
`result.gate`: `level`, `verdict` (`pass`, `fail` or `not_run`),
`commands`, each with `name`, `exit_code`, `seconds`, `log` and, when it
failed, `tail`, and more (`docs/speca.md`).

**Published schemas and skill text.** `29_af_spec_under_controller`
publishes `af-spec-result.v1.json` and sets the conventions this package
follows: the common members of a result, a schema per skill, tests beside
the schemas in the test-only Go package under `specification/schemas/`,
and the skill's behaviour carried in task steps because skill text is not
tested (steering, ADR 12).

**The controller this is written for.** nightshift starts implementer
sessions (`af-impl`) with `claude -p` in a clone of a task fork on a Parley
hub. The session's credential can fetch and push in the fork and nothing
else: it cannot write the base branch and has no forge token. The hub
records every push of the branch as a version of a change, refuses to land
a merge commit, and lands the change itself after nightshift's gate and a
reviewer passed it.

## Requirements

Constraint: Linux and macOS; Windows is best effort. Constraint: `af-impl`
run without any argument this package adds behaves exactly as it does
today. Constraint: in this mode, the mode's rules on branches, merging and
pushing take the place of the repository's own agent instructions
(`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`) on those points; every other instruction of the
repository still holds.

### The result file

`--result <file>` is accepted by `af-impl` with `--no-merge`. Given without
it, the skill says `--result needs --unattended, --no-merge or --rework`
and does nothing.

The file is one JSON document, written once, as the last thing the run
does, outside the repository's working tree when the path is outside it.
Every document has:

- `skill`: `af-impl`; `mode`: `no_merge`;
- `outcome`: one of the values named below;
- `reason`: one sentence, present when the outcome is a refusal or
  `push_failed`;
- `package`: `spec_dir`, `spec_id`, `spec_name`, `title`, `status`,
  `profile`, absent when the run refused before it knew the package;
- `branch` and `head`: the branch the run worked on and its last commit,
  and `pushed`: whether that commit is on `origin`;
- the members named below.

A run that refuses before it changes anything still writes the file, with
the refusal as `outcome` and `reason`. A path that cannot be written is
said in the session's last message (`result file not written: <error>`);
the run's work is left as it is. A caller treats a session that left no
file, or one that does not parse, as failed.

Without `--result` the mode behaves the same and reports in the session
only.

### af-impl: stop at the pushed branch

`af-impl <package> --no-merge` implements the package on the branch that
is checked out, and ends when that branch is pushed. It combines with
`--unattended`. `--base <branch>` names the base branch; without it, the
base is the default branch of `origin`.

What differs from a run without it:

- **Where it starts.** The checked-out branch is the work branch. It must
  not be the base branch (`refused_branch`, `checked out on the base
  branch <name>`), and the package must be on it. The branch may already
  hold commits ahead of the base: the package's own, and earlier work of
  the same package, which the run continues as §4 describes. The run
  creates no branch.
- **The forge.** The run calls no forge command. The survey reads no open
  items, and says so in its brief. No issue is opened, closed, commented
  on or relabelled.
- **The dependencies.** A dependency of the package that is neither sealed
  nor has its last task `done`, judged on the work branch, refuses the
  run (`refused_dependency`, naming the package).
- **The end.** After the conformance pass the run takes
  `speca <package> --gate full` on the tip of the work branch. On a
  landable verdict it pushes the work branch to `origin` and stops there,
  on the work branch. It does not check out, merge into, or push the base
  branch.
- **The record.** What the merge commit's message would have held (the
  open items, the deviations, one entry per task, the verification, the
  conformance findings) is written into the result as `summary`, as
  Markdown, and the numbers of the `AF-Run:` trailer as `run`.

The outcomes:

- `complete`: every task is `done` or `dropped`, the full gate is
  landable, the branch is pushed, and no open item remains;
- `complete_with_open_items`: the same, with a non-empty `open_items`;
- `parked`: a task failed twice. Its `wip:` commit stays at the tip of the
  work branch, which is pushed; `parked` holds the task's number and the
  check's output;
- `gate_failed`: every task is done and the full gate on the tip is not
  landable. The branch is pushed; `gate` holds what each command returned;
- `push_failed`: the push was refused; `reason` is git's message, and the
  commits stay local;
- a refusal: `refused_branch`, `refused_dependency`, `refused_dirty` (the
  working tree is not clean), `refused_package` (a required file is
  missing, the package does not validate, its status is not `draft` or
  `active`, its intent or contract drifted, or `speca` refuses the first
  task move; `reason` says which), each changing nothing.

The result also holds `tasks` (per task: `number`, `outcome`, `commit`,
the gate `verdict`), `deviations` (each with its key, its reason and the
ADR that records it) and `open_items`: the `unmet` list, one entry per
open item, with `kind` (`awaits`, `defect`, `untested` or `deviation`),
`severity` for a defect, `awaits` (the package id) for an `awaits` item,
`title` (at most 60 characters, as the issue's title would be), `missing`,
`why`, `ids`, `evidence`, `adr` where there is one, and `closes` (what
would close it). An outbound handoff its receiver does not take yet is an
`awaits` entry, as in a landing.

Running the same command again on a branch that was parked, or whose push
failed, continues it, as a run without `--no-merge` continues its branch.

### End-to-end flow

**An implementation handed over.** After the person approved the plan, the
controller activates the package on the branch and starts `af-impl
.specs/62_<name> --unattended --no-merge --result impl.json`. The run
surveys without the forge, implements each task in a subagent with its
evidence recorded, writes the documentation, runs the conformance pass and
the full gate, pushes the branch and writes `impl.json` with `outcome:
complete_with_open_items` and one `untested` item. The base branch is as
it was, and no issue exists.

## Design Decisions

1. **The result is a file, at a path the caller gives, and a refusal
   writes it too.** As in `29_af_spec_under_controller`.
2. **`--no-merge` runs the full gate on the branch tip, not on a merged
   tree.** There is no merged tree; the caller that lands the work gates
   what it lands.
3. **A parked or gate-failed branch is pushed.** Unfinished first work is
   lost with the clone unless it is pushed.
4. **The mode's rules on branches and merging outrank the repository's
   agent instructions.** Those instructions commonly say "merge into main
   and push it", which is exactly what the caller asked the skill not to
   do.
5. **The result has a published JSON Schema, `af-impl-result.v1.json`, and
   the package's criteria are about it.** The owner decided it for the
   three packages of this PRD: skill text cannot be tested, and an active
   package closes a task only on a test per criterion.
6. **The skill's behaviour is carried in the task steps, and in
   `skills/af-impl/references/no-merge.md`.** The body of `SKILL.md` is at
   its ceiling, and a reference file loads only in the runs that use the
   mode.
7. **Profile: `lite`.** Three requirements, each about what the schema
   accepts and refuses; the end-to-end flow passes through a model session,
   which no smoke check can run.
8. **`reason` is required for every `refused_*` outcome and for
   `push_failed`.** `parked` and `gate_failed` carry the check's output and
   the gate in its place.
9. **`complete`, `complete_with_open_items`, `parked` and `gate_failed`
   mean the tip is on `origin`** (`pushed: true`); `push_failed` means it
   is not. A document that says otherwise is refused by the schema.
10. **A run that got past its refusals always carries `package`, `tasks`,
    `deviations` and `open_items`**, each list possibly empty; `summary`
    and `run` are required for the two `complete` outcomes and for
    `gate_failed`, where every task is done and the record exists, and are
    optional for `parked` and `push_failed`.
11. **A task's `outcome` in the result is its state**: `done`, `dropped`,
    `in_progress` for the parked one, or `pending` for those after it. A
    done task carries its `commit` and its gate `verdict`, one of `pass`,
    `pass_baseline_failing`, `regressed`, `still_failing` and
    `gate_failed`: the five rows of the table in §5 of the skill.
12. **`run` is the `AF-Run:` trailer's object**: `gate`, as `speca
    --gate-report` gives it, and `open_items`, whose `opened` counts the
    result's open items by kind, a defect as `defect:<severity>`, and whose
    `closed`, `passed_on` and `reclassified` are empty, because the run
    reads and writes no issue.
13. **`gate` is `speca`'s `result.gate` object, copied**: the schema
    requires its `verdict` and its `commands`, each with `name`,
    `exit_code` and `seconds`, and lets the object carry what else `speca`
    puts there, so that a new member of the gate's answer does not make a
    result invalid. Everywhere else the schema refuses a member it does not
    name.
14. **`parked` is `{task, output}`**: the task's number and the output of
    the check that failed.
15. **An open item's `ids` and `evidence` are lists of strings**, `ids`
    non-empty; `adr` is the ADR's path; `awaits` is the receiving package's
    id as its directory spells it (`"31"`).
16. **A deviation always names its ADR.** The skill records every declared
    deviation in one (§5, step 8); where the repository's instructions put
    decisions elsewhere, `adr` is that document's path.
17. **In a package that requires evidence, the run takes `speca <package>
    --verify-evidence` on the tip after the full gate**, as a landing does
    on the merged tree. A `fail` is a verdict that is not landable: the
    outcome is `gate_failed`, and `summary` names the tests that failed.
18. **`--base` names a branch of `origin`**, and the base is used to tell
    the work branch from it, to measure the diff of the conformance pass
    and for the gate's base; the run fetches it and never checks it out.
19. **The package is "on the branch" when `speca <package>` resolves it in
    the checked-out tree.** Otherwise the run is refused with
    `refused_package`, as for a missing file.
20. **`refused_package` and `refused_dependency` name the package they
    looked at** when they could read it, so `package` may be present on a
    refusal, with any lifecycle status.
21. **The reference documentation is `docs/controller.md`**, which
    `29_af_spec_under_controller` creates: this package adds `--no-merge`,
    `--base`, the outcomes and the schema to it, and `docs/architecture.md`
    lists the schema file.

## Dependencies

- **`29_af_spec_under_controller`** (`draft`): the result file's common
  members and the conventions of its schema and tests, which this package
  follows.
- **`27_unattended_mode`** (`active`): `af-impl --unattended`, which
  `--no-merge` combines with and does not change.
- **`21_open_item_labels`**, **`22_open_items_read_back`** (`active`): the
  kinds of an open item, which the result's `open_items` carry, and the
  survey's read of open items, which `--no-merge` leaves out.
- **`19_speca_gate`** (`active`): the full gate and its answer, which the
  result copies.
- **`20_specrun_driver`** (`active`): unchanged; it calls `af-impl` without
  the new arguments.
- **nightshift** (`agent-fox-dev/nightshift`,
  `docs/prd/02-drive-work-items-through-the-hub.md`): the first caller of
  this mode. It depends on this package; nothing here depends on it.

## Verified External API

- **`claude -p`**, read in `docs/specrun.md`: `claude -p "/af-impl
  <spec_dir> --unattended" --output-format stream-json --verbose`, the
  call `specrun` makes and a controller makes with the new arguments.
- **`speca`**, read in `docs/speca.md` and the skills:
  `speca <package> --validate`, `speca <package> --gate task|full`,
  `speca <package> --gate-report --since <commit>`,
  `speca <package> --verify-evidence`,
  `speca <package> --task <N> --state <S>`. `evidence_required` is `true`
  for an active package with a `contract_hash`.
- **`github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6`** v6.0.2, in `go.mod`:
  `jsonschema.NewCompiler()`, `(*Compiler).Compile(path)`,
  `jsonschema.UnmarshalJSON(reader)`, `(*Schema).Validate(value)`.

## Glossary

- **controller**: a program that starts skill sessions, reads their result
  files and lands their work itself; nightshift is one.
- **work branch**: the branch a controller checked out for one piece of
  work, which a skill run commits to and pushes.
- **result file**: the JSON document a run writes at the path `--result`
  names, saying how it ended.
- **open item, `unmet`, kind, severity**: as `af-impl`'s conformance pass
  defines them (`skills/af-impl/references/conformance.md`).
- **package, draft, active, `lite`, gate, evidence**: as the spec format
  and `docs/speca.md` define them.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Say how a run that stopped at the pushed branch ended

**Rationale:** The controller lands the work, files the open items and starts the next step from this file alone.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] THE af-impl result schema SHALL for any result document of a `--no-merge` run that got past its refusals, accept it: `skill` is `af-impl`, `mode` is `no_merge`, `outcome` is `complete`, `complete_with_open_items`, `parked`, `gate_failed` or `push_failed`, `package` holds its six members, `branch` and `head` are non-empty strings, `pushed` is a boolean, and `tasks`, `deviations` and `open_items` are lists
   → validating the document against the schema returns no error
   Check: unit
   - setup: the schema compiled from specification/schemas/af-impl-result.v1.json with github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6, by the helper specification/schemas/af_spec_result_test.go already has
   - setup: a base document built in the test: skill 'af-impl', mode 'no_merge', outcome 'complete', a package of spec_dir '.specs/62_retry_budget', spec_id '62', spec_name 'retry_budget', a title, status 'active' and profile 'full', branch 'work/62', a 40-digit hex head, pushed true, tasks holding {number: 1, outcome: 'done', commit, verdict: 'pass'}, empty deviations and open_items, a summary, and run holding the gate and open_items objects of the AF-Run trailer that skills/af-impl/references/landing.md shows, with opened {}
   ```
   in specification/schemas/af_impl_result_test.go (new), one table of documents the schema accepts, each the base document with a change: {unchanged; a package of status 'draft' and profile 'lite'; outcome 'complete_with_open_items' with open_items [{kind: 'untested', title: 'no test of the retry cap', missing, why, ids: ['REQ-2.3'], evidence: ['retry/budget.go:41'], closes}]; outcome 'parked' with parked {task: 2, output}, tasks of outcomes done, in_progress and pending, and neither summary nor run; outcome 'gate_failed' with gate {level: 'full', verdict: 'fail', commands: [{name: 'all_tests', exit_code: 1, seconds: 3.2, tail}]}; outcome 'push_failed' with pushed false and a reason; outcome 'push_failed' with pushed false, a reason and neither summary nor run; each of refused_branch, refused_dependency, refused_dirty and refused_package with a reason and no package, tasks, deviations, open_items, summary or run; refused_package with a reason and a package of status 'sealed'; refused_dependency with a reason, a package and pushed false}: assert schema.Validate(document) returns no error
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] WHEN a result document's `outcome` is `refused_branch`, `refused_dependency`, `refused_dirty` or `refused_package` and it carries a non-empty `reason`, THE af-impl result schema SHALL accept the document without `package`, `tasks`, `deviations`, `open_items`, `summary` and `run`, with `pushed` either `true` or `false`, and with a `package` of any lifecycle status when it carries one
   → validating the document returns no error
   Check: same as REQ-1.1
1. [REQ-1.3] IF a result document lacks `skill`, `mode`, `outcome`, `branch`, `head` or `pushed`, or its `skill` is not `af-impl`, its `mode` is not `no_merge`, its `outcome` is none of `complete`, `complete_with_open_items`, `parked`, `gate_failed`, `push_failed`, `refused_branch`, `refused_dependency`, `refused_dirty` and `refused_package`, its `branch` or `head` is empty, its `pushed` is not a boolean, or it carries a member the schema does not name, THEN THE af-impl result schema SHALL refuse the document
   → validating the document returns an error whose text names the member that is missing, wrong or unknown
   Check: unit
   - setup: the schema compiled from specification/schemas/af-impl-result.v1.json with github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6, by the helper specification/schemas/af_spec_result_test.go already has
   - setup: a base document built in the test: skill 'af-impl', mode 'no_merge', outcome 'complete', a package of spec_dir '.specs/62_retry_budget', spec_id '62', spec_name 'retry_budget', a title, status 'active' and profile 'full', branch 'work/62', a 40-digit hex head, pushed true, tasks holding {number: 1, outcome: 'done', commit, verdict: 'pass'}, empty deviations and open_items, a summary, and run holding the gate and open_items objects of the AF-Run trailer that skills/af-impl/references/landing.md shows, with opened {}
   ```
   in specification/schemas/af_impl_result_test.go, one table of documents the schema refuses, each the base document with one change and the member the error must name: {skill, mode, outcome, branch, head and pushed removed in turn; skill 'af-spec'; mode 'unattended'; outcome 'written'; outcome 'merged'; branch ''; head ''; pushed 1; an added member 'merge_commit'; outcome 'refused_branch' without reason; outcome 'refused_dirty' with reason ''; outcome 'push_failed' with pushed false and no reason; package, tasks, deviations and open_items removed in turn; package.status 'sealed'; package.profile 'small'; summary removed; run removed; outcome 'gate_failed' with a gate and no summary; outcome 'complete' with open_items [{kind: 'untested', title: 'no test of the retry cap', missing, why, ids: ['REQ-2.3'], evidence: ['retry/budget.go:41'], closes}]; outcome 'complete_with_open_items' with open_items []; pushed false on the base; outcome 'parked' with parked {task: 2, output} and pushed false; outcome 'gate_failed' with a gate and pushed false; outcome 'push_failed' with a reason and pushed true; outcome 'parked' without parked; parked {task: 2} and parked {output} and parked {task: 0, output}; outcome 'gate_failed' without gate; outcome 'complete' with a gate of verdict 'fail'}: assert schema.Validate(document) returns an error, and that the error's text names the member the case gives
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] IF a result document's `outcome` begins `refused_` or is `push_failed` and it has no `reason`, or an empty one, THEN THE af-impl result schema SHALL refuse the document
   → validating the document returns an error that names `reason`
   Check: same as REQ-1.3
1. [REQ-1.5] IF a result document's `outcome` is `complete`, `complete_with_open_items`, `parked`, `gate_failed` or `push_failed` and it lacks `package`, `tasks`, `deviations` or `open_items`, or its `package.status` is neither `draft` nor `active`, or its `outcome` is `complete`, `complete_with_open_items` or `gate_failed` and it lacks `summary` or `run`, THEN THE af-impl result schema SHALL refuse the document
   → validating the document returns an error that names the missing or wrong member
   Check: same as REQ-1.3
1. [REQ-1.6] IF a result document's `outcome` is `complete` and its `open_items` is not empty, or its `outcome` is `complete_with_open_items` and its `open_items` is empty, THEN THE af-impl result schema SHALL refuse the document
   → validating the document returns an error that names `open_items`
   Check: same as REQ-1.3
1. [REQ-1.7] IF a result document's `outcome` is `complete`, `complete_with_open_items`, `parked` or `gate_failed` and its `pushed` is `false`, or its `outcome` is `push_failed` and its `pushed` is `true`, THEN THE af-impl result schema SHALL refuse the document
   → validating the document returns an error that names `pushed`
   Check: same as REQ-1.3
1. [REQ-1.8] IF a result document's `outcome` is `parked` and it has no `parked` member holding a `task` of at least 1 and an `output`, or its `outcome` is `gate_failed` and it has no `gate`, or its `outcome` is `complete` or `complete_with_open_items` and it carries a `gate` whose `verdict` is not `pass`, THEN THE af-impl result schema SHALL refuse the document
   → validating the document returns an error that names `parked` or `gate`
   Check: same as REQ-1.3

### REQ-2: Carry the record a merge commit would have held

**Rationale:** Without a merge commit, the tasks, the deviations and the gate's numbers have no other place a caller can read them from.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] THE af-impl result schema SHALL for any result document whose `tasks`, `deviations`, `run` and `gate` are as a run writes them, accept it: a task entry holds `number`, at least 1, and `outcome`, one of `done`, `dropped`, `in_progress` and `pending`, and a `done` one also `commit` and `verdict`, one of `pass`, `pass_baseline_failing`, `regressed`, `still_failing` and `gate_failed`; a deviation holds `key`, `reason` and `adr`; `run` holds `gate` and `open_items`; `gate` holds `verdict` and `commands`
   → validating the document returns no error, and a `gate` object may carry members of `speca`'s gate answer the schema does not name

# Tasks

## Test Commands

- **all_tests:** `make test`
- **linter:** `make lint`
- **spec_tests:** `go test ./specification/... -count=1`

## Dependencies

- `29` — the result file's common members, the conventions of its schema, and the test-only package and its helper under specification/schemas/
- `27` — af-impl --unattended, which --no-merge combines with and does not change
- `21` — the kinds and severities of an open item, which the result's open_items carry
- `22` — the survey's read of open items from the forge, which --no-merge leaves out
- `19` — the full gate and the shape of its answer, which the result copies

## Tasks

### 1. Publish the af-impl result schema and start a run on the checked-out branch (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Add the two tables of the result's behaviours, accepted and refused documents, to specification/schemas/af_impl_result_test.go in the test-only package beside the schemas, each case built from one base document and compiled with the helper the af-spec result's tests use, and confirm both fail because the schema does not exist
- 1.2 Write specification/schemas/af-impl-result.v1.json in the style of af-spec-result.v1.json: the $id https://agent-fox.dev/schemas/af-impl-result.v1.json, a description on every member, additionalProperties false; the common members, the nine outcomes of the mode no_merge, and the rules of the criteria on reason, package, tasks, deviations, open_items, summary, run, pushed, parked and gate. tasks, deviations and open_items are lists and run and gate objects here; the shape of what they hold comes with the later tasks
- 1.3 Add skills/af-impl/references/no-merge.md and link it from §1 of skills/af-impl/SKILL.md in one sentence: `<package> --no-merge` implements the package on the branch that is checked out and ends when that branch is pushed; it combines with --unattended; --base <branch> names the base branch, a branch of origin, and without it the base is origin's default branch. The run fetches the base and never checks it out; it uses it to tell the work branch from it, for the diff the conformance pass measures and as the gate's base
- 1.4 In that file, where the run starts, in place of §2's branch check and all of §4: the checked-out branch is the work branch; it must not be the base branch, refused_branch with `checked out on the base branch <name>`; the package must resolve with speca in the checked-out tree; the branch may already hold commits ahead of the base, the package's own and earlier work of the same package, which the run continues as §4 describes, dropping a wip: commit at the tip; the run creates no branch and switches to none
- 1.5 In that file, the refusals, each before anything is changed and each with a reason that says which: refused_dirty for a working tree that is not clean; refused_package for a required file that is missing, a package speca cannot resolve on the branch or that does not validate, a status that is not draft or active, intent or contract drift, or a refused dry run of the first task move; refused_dependency, naming the package, for a dependency that is neither sealed nor has its last task done, judged with speca on the work branch
- 1.6 In that file, the forge: the run calls no forge command, neither issue nor gh nor glab; the survey reads no open items and its brief says so in the place where references/survey.md lists them; no issue is opened, closed, commented on or relabelled
- 1.7 Say in that file that its rules on branches, merging and pushing take the place of the repository's agent instructions on those points and that every other instruction of the repository still holds, and that a run without --no-merge is unchanged
- 1.8 In SKILL.md, name `<package> --no-merge [--base <branch>] [--result <file>]` in the argument hint and keep the body under the ceiling `make skills-check` enforces by moving text into a reference file, never by dropping a rule

**Touches:**

- `specification/schemas/af-impl-result.v1.json`
- `specification/schemas/af_impl_result_test.go`
- `skills/af-impl/references/no-merge.md`
- `skills/af-impl/SKILL.md`

**Done when:**

- the checks of the criteria listed above exist as tests, are executable and pass
- `make test` passes
- `make lint` passes
- `make skills-check` passes

### 2. End the run at the push and write its record into the result (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-2

**Steps:**

- 2.1 Add the cases of tasks, deviations, run and gate to the two tables of specification/schemas/af_impl_result_test.go and confirm the new cases fail
- 2.2 Extend specification/schemas/af-impl-result.v1.json with the entries of tasks and deviations and the objects run and gate, as the criteria give them; gate is the one object that may carry members the schema does not name, since it is speca's answer copied
- 2.3 In skills/af-impl/references/no-merge.md, the end, in place of §7 and references/landing.md: after the conformance pass the run takes `speca <package> --gate full` on the tip of the work branch and, in a package that requires evidence, `speca <package> --verify-evidence` after it; on a landable verdict of both it pushes the work branch to origin and stops there, on the work branch. It does not check out, merge into or push the base branch, runs no merge and writes no merge commit
- 2.4 In that file, the record: what the merge commit's message would have held, section by section as references/landing.md gives it (the open items first, the deviations, one entry per task with its commit, files, test verdicts and criterion-to-test map, the verification with the gate report, the conformance findings), is written as Markdown into summary; run is the object of the AF-Run trailer, its gate copied from `speca <package> --gate-report --since <baseline commit>` and its open_items.opened counting the result's open items by kind, a defect as defect:<severity>, with closed, passed_on and reclassified empty
- 2.5 In that file, the outcomes: complete when every task is done or dropped, both verdicts are landable, the branch is pushed and no open item remains; complete_with_open_items the same with open items; parked when a task failed twice, its wip: commit staying at the tip of the work branch, which is pushed, with the task's number and the check's output; gate_failed when every task is done and the full gate or the evidence check on the tip is not landable, the branch pushed all the same and gate holding speca's answer; push_failed when the push is refused, with git's message, the commits staying local. A parked run stays on the work branch instead of returning to the base branch
- 2.6 In that file, the result: --result <file> is taken with --no-merge, and without it or --rework the skill says `--result needs --unattended, --no-merge or --rework` and does nothing; the document is written once, as the last thing the run does, also after a refusal; name every member and what the run puts in it, a task's outcome being its state and its verdict the row of §5's table, and point at the schema file; a path that cannot be written is said in the last message as `result file not written: <error>` and the work is left as it is; without --result the run behaves the same and reports in the session only
- 2.7 In that file, continuing: the same command run again on a branch that was parked, or whose push failed, continues it as §4 continues a branch
- 2.8 In SKILL.md, say in *Run to the end* and in *Never* in one clause each that with --no-merge the run ends at the push of the work branch and commits nothing to the base branch, keeping the body under the ceiling

- `specification/schemas/af_impl_result_test.go`

### 3. Hand the open items to the caller in place of the forge (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-3

- 3.2 Extend specification/schemas/af-impl-result.v1.json with the entry of open_items: kind, severity on a defect only, awaits on an awaits item only, a title of at most 60 characters, missing, why, ids, evidence, adr where there is one, and closes
- 3.3 In skills/af-impl/references/no-merge.md, the open items: every entry of the unmet list of references/conformance.md is one entry of open_items, with the kind and, for a defect, the severity the conformance pass gave it; title is what the issue's title would say after `<NN_name>: `, in at most 60 characters; missing and why are the entry's words; ids are the ids it concerns; evidence is its file:line references and check output; adr is the ADR that records the decision, where there is one; closes says what would close it, and for an awaits item names the receiving package
- 3.4 In that file, the handoffs: each outbound handoff of the package that its receiver does not take yet is an awaits entry, awaits holding the receiver's id, as in a landing; when `speca <MM>` says the receiver is sealed or its last task is done, the entry is a defect of severity correctness with the note `handoff to a package that has already landed`
- 3.5 In that file, what the mode leaves out of a landing: no issue is looked for or opened, nothing the survey would have listed is closed, and nothing that awaited this package is passed on; the report of §8 lists the open items from the result in place of issue links, and says that whoever lands the work files them
- 3.6 In references/conformance.md, say in one clause where it names §7 that with --no-merge the unmet list goes to the result; in SKILL.md say the same in §6 and in the last entry of *Never*, keeping the body under the ceiling; run `make skills-check`
